correctness.rationale: For stationary binary latent Markov process, covariance at lag h is pi(1-pi)lambda^h; independent noisy emissions multiply cross-season covariance by (d_i-f)(d_j-f). Equality of normalized adjacent covariances yields a unique f since c01-c12 = pi(1-pi)(d1-f)lambda(d0-d2) != 0. Exact ratios then recover lambda, pi, d_t, gamma and epsilon, with direct substitution proving the feasibility converse. When outer rates coincide, f can vary on an open interval while all six moments remain fixed; when lambda=0, full observations factor. Full hidden/observed eight-state rational enumeration reproduces exact inversion in twelve interior cases, and a separate distinct-model boundary certificate passes.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge original sharp design boundary and explicit six-moment inverse for a stationary dynamic ecological occupancy model with unknown common positive false-positive probability and seasonally varying true-positive detection, conditional on differing outer rates. Published same-object approaches treat occupancy mixture estimation, variable-state mislocation errors, homogeneous binary HMMs, or general full-law identifiability; none of their inspected statements supplies this moment-level inverse. Inaccessible primary full text and terminology overlap remain acknowledged originality risks.

value.rationale: Addresses the practical ecological uncertainty created by nonzero false detections without within-season repeat visits. Supplies an exact sharp observation-design criterion that breaks the common false-alarm/occupancy ambiguity, a constructive parameter inverse, feasible-moment test, and a boundary continuum showing why unchanged outer detection effort is insufficient at the level of first and second moments. The result is mathematically more than a routine substitution of f=0: that simplification removes an unknown confounded rate, so a new rank condition and proof are necessary. It is not a claim about efficient finite-sample estimation or general ecological forecast skill.
